judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema's 'catch-all' index signatures are computed from zod schema .toString() calls, which do not produce usable keys (e.g. '[object Object]'), so the schema is not a wildcard matcher the comment claims ('any property with a number is the expiry'). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, token responses with extra numeric fields or unexpected shapes are validated against a schema that does not do what the code comments and callers assume; the expiry_date field the Google/Office365 paths read afterwards will be undefined, and any future test suite mocking a realistic token response would silently exercise a different schema than the code's intent.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to express “any numeric property” via computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those computed property names evaluate to a single literal string (likely `"[object Object]"`), not a wildcard/catch-all. So when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is on, `safeParse(response)` will not validate arbitrary token-response shapes as the comments/callers imply, and can either (a) reject legitimate responses (throwing `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`) or (b) fail to ensure fields like `expiry_date` exist/are numeric. This is directly introduced by the diff and affects new call sites (e.g., Google/Office365 using `parseRefreshTokenResponse`).
